node_that_feeds_something_else.why: an input the node substitutes is still a valid share of a different number, and every commitment it opens still opens. That is zk/input_check.py, which catches the node where this catches the dealer. Neither implies the other.

composes_with_the_input_check.question: BINDING.md said the two catch different parties and compose in principle, and that they had never been run together.
composes_with_the_input_check.answer: they compose. All four arms verified against the cleartext reference on the same market.
composes_with_the_input_check.the_check_costs: the aggregate one round and about six kilobytes; the per-party two rounds and 0.28 MB, which is one opening a node rather than one for all of them. That is what buys naming the node instead of only detecting that somebody substituted.
composes_with_the_input_check.what_the_pair_now_covers: the dealer, by the share commitments, and the node, by the input check. Neither implies the other and both now run at once.
composes_with_the_input_check.note: the first version of this table quoted the aggregate's cost under the heading `--input-check`, which was the default at the time and is not sound. Both are measured here and labelled.
